issues.description: Entire script file slurped into RPC response and stored in React state for every compile
issues.detail: The backend now reads script_content unconditionally and ships it across the RPC boundary, then the frontend keeps it in component state. Pipelines can be large; you've made every compile pay a memory and serialization cost just so a button can call Blob(). A download endpoint that streams the file on click is the right shape.

issues.description: open() without encoding or error handling on a path you just wrote
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding and has no try/except. The compiled script is text the tool generated; pin encoding='utf-8' and handle IOError so a read failure doesn't tank the whole compile response after the pipeline already succeeded. Cheap fix, refuse the patch without it.

issues.description: Two sources of truth for the file: disk path and in-memory blob
issues.detail: compiledPath already points at the file on disk. Now compiledContent carries a second copy of the same bytes in the browser. They can diverge, they double the memory, and the existing anchor next to the new icon already links to the artifact. Pick one. Either serve the file via URL or drop the path.

issues.description: Download icon is a bare icon with onClick, not a button
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick isn't keyboard-focusable and isn't announced as a control. The sibling 'Done' status uses an anchor. Use an IconButton or an anchor with download attribute so tab order and screen readers behave. titleAccess alone doesn't make it a button.

issues.description: Filename fallback 'pipeline.kale.py' will never trigger and hides intent
issues.detail: split('/').pop() on a non-empty compiledPath always yields a non-empty string, so the || branch is dead. If you actually care about the empty case, guard the handler earlier. Dead branches in trivial code are a taste smell, not a safety net.

issues.description: Commit/PR does two things: backend payload change and frontend UI addition
issues.detail: Backend RPC contract change and a new UI affordance are two patches. Splitting them makes the RPC change reviewable on its own merits (which, as noted, are weak) and keeps the UI patch honest. THREE-PATCHES-adjacent, but at minimum two.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The feature is fine; the shape is wrong. You're shoving the entire compiled script through the RPC response and into React state so a button can wrap it in a Blob, when the file already exists on disk and compiledPath already references it. Add a download endpoint (or use the existing path with a proper anchor + download attribute) and stop duplicating bytes. Also: pin the file encoding, handle read failures, make the icon an actual button, and split the backend contract change from the UI patch. Good intent, bad taste — special-cases an in-memory copy when the general path (serve the file) already exists.
